components: Analysis 1: Analysis on the Real Line
Study theories of learning and mathematical communication, then develop a group teaching or communication project with a report and presentation.

Selected six-credit mathematics option in year two. Combinatorial counting uses generating functions, recurrence equations and formal power series; earlier groups, rings and fields provide the recommended background.
Selected six-credit mathematics option in year two. Complex differentiation, contour integration, residues and Taylor and Laurent series build on the earlier analysis courses.

Six genuinely free credits in year two and twenty-four in year three remain open. Selection needs Examination Board approval for overlap and level; programme mathematics options are approved. Normally at most twelve free credits may be introductory. UvA and VU minors have the stated introductory-level exception.
Examine ethical and societal questions in mathematics, including financial models, cryptography, privacy, algorithms and AI.

Entry requires at least 132 credits from the Mathematics programme. The example completes 120 credits in years one and two and eighteen restricted mathematics credits in the first two periods of year three before the January project start. Individually supervised research produces a thesis, presentation and oral defence.
Selected six-credit mathematics option in the first semester of year three. Study probability-based entropy, compression, coding and security, including proofs.
Selected six-credit mathematics option in the first semester of year three. Smooth manifolds, differential forms and integration build on analysis, linear algebra and topology.
Selected six-credit mathematics option in the first semester of year three. Study infinite-dimensional linear spaces and mappings, building on compulsory analysis and linear algebra.

Twenty-four free credits remain open. A thirty-credit minor or approved foreign semester has separate redistribution rules, including a mathematics choice in year two and a conditional replacement of Reflection on Mathematics. This example retains the ordinary route and Reflection course.

core: Calculus, rigorous mathematical analysis and proof
Linear algebra and abstract algebraic structures
Discrete mathematics, logic and mathematical reasoning
Probability theory, mathematical statistics and stochastic systems
Differential equations, iteration and mathematical modelling
Mathematical modelling of real systems and solving real-world problems with mathematics
Programming, numerical methods and mathematical software
Reflection, communication and mathematical research practice
Independent bachelor research project in mathematics
questions: How can mathematical models describe change in systems such as epidemics, traffic flows and climate?
How can mathematics reveal patterns in data and improve concrete planning or financial decisions?
How does mathematics contribute to artificial intelligence, secure communication and other future technologies?

trace: Mandatory first-year development and academic research literacy.
Discounted cash flows, NPV/IRR, cost of capital and accounting-based investment appraisal support finance applications; no derivative-pricing claim.
Algebraic/graphical economic analysis, consumer/game theory and IS-LM introduce economic modelling.
Macroeconomic market dynamics, expectations and IS-LM-PC models extend the economic-system application.
Choice under uncertainty, strategic behaviour and equilibrium models support formal economic reasoning.
Economic efficiency/equity models, policy data and research develop a specific public-policy model application.
Description-supported OLS/GLS/IV, statistical tests, Monte Carlo simulation and an empirical paper implement econometric estimation.
Empirical research design, sampling, inference and an original team-data project supply applied statistical methods.
Algorithmic fairness, privacy, responsibility and ethical-framework analysis supply specific reflection on mathematical AI applications.
Bayesian/temporal probabilistic models, expected utility and Markov decision processes directly develop decisions under uncertainty.
Formal logic, sets, relations, quantifiers, direct/indirect proofs and induction directly implement mathematical reasoning.
Search, first/second-order optimisation, constraints, linear programming and experimental algorithm evaluation develop optimisation methods.
Description-supported reinforcement algorithms and learning agents provide a sequential-decision application in the economics/optimisation programme.
Description-supported relational theory, normalization, SQL and query processing supply data organization for statistical inquiry.
C++/functional Haskell construction, debugging and testing support reliable implementation of computational models; not a pure-mathematics course.
Asymptotic analysis, graph algorithms, computability and reductions connect discrete reasoning with algorithm implementation.
Exact arithmetic, number-theoretic/matrix/Fourier algorithms, dynamic programming and network flows provide advanced computational mathematics.
R data transformation, joining and visualization support empirical/model research workflows.
Regression/classification, regularisation, resampling, dimensionality reduction and test-set evaluation implement statistical learning.
Spatial/spectral image representations, transforms, filters and recognition pipelines apply mathematical computation to image data.
Gradient descent, backpropagation and network implementation apply mathematical/statistical tools to prediction.
Coordinate transformations, kinematics, configuration spaces, collision/motion planning and robot programming supply a substantial geometric/computational application.
Python programming, recursion and testing implement computational problem-solving.
Single-variable calculus, Taylor approximation and dynamic-model implementation form the analytical foundation.
Vector spaces, transformations, eigenvalues, least squares and SVD support mathematical modelling and data methods.
Numerical root finding, quadrature, ODEs and linear/nonlinear systems explicitly address convergence, error, stability and sensitivity.
Description-supported multivariable calculus, differential equations and complex-valued functions extend analytical methods; no undocumented theorem sequence claimed.
Differential/difference equations, convolution, transforms, filtering and feedback provide a sustained linear-system mathematical application.
Probability spaces, multivariate distributions, inference, likelihood, Bayesian reasoning and sampling-algorithm project supply rigorous probability/statistics.
Population dynamics, energy/matter calculations and dedicated ecological modelling in R provide an actual applied modelling setting.
Spatial data models, coordinate transformations, spectral sensing and geospatial case analysis implement environmental data inquiry.
Description-supported Earth-system modelling and tracer-based climate inquiry extend the model application, without inventing its methods or assessment.
Difference/first-order differential-equation models, rates, uncertainty and scientific measurements support the environmental modelling application and formal progression.
Disease rates, association, confounding and population-data interpretation provide a concrete quantitative health application, not an ODE-simulation course.
Multivariable statistical models, diagnostics, repeated-measures designs, categorical/latent constructs and R papers deepen applied inference.

alternatives.label: Mathematics, modelling & computation
alternatives.labelReason: Reviewed completed mathematical/computational core and actual application weights; label describes these fields without claiming the full pure-mathematics sequence.
alternatives.concept: Combine calculus, linear algebra, formal proof, probability, numerical methods and linear systems with algorithm design and optimisation. Apply these mathematical tools through robotics, ecological and Earth-system models, image analysis and statistical computation.
progression: All current term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass. Introductory programming precedes dependent algorithms and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes all dependent mathematics. Numerical methods and Linear Systems follow foundational mathematics. Some image-processing work precedes later matrix courses under the open curriculum; no extra formal prerequisite is invented. Data alternative uses advanced algorithms rather than placing Reinforcement Learning before a later neural-network foundation.

alternatives.label: Mathematics, statistics & data science
alternatives.labelReason: Reviewed completed mathematical/computational core and actual application weights; label describes these fields without claiming the full pure-mathematics sequence.
alternatives.concept: Develop mathematical and statistical reasoning through calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and algorithms, then use these foundations for inference, econometrics, data management and machine learning. Image, satellite and population-health data provide concrete applications, with attention to responsible algorithm use.
progression: All current term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass. Introductory programming precedes dependent algorithms and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes all dependent mathematics. Numerical methods and Linear Systems follow foundational mathematics. Some image-processing work precedes later matrix courses under the open curriculum; no extra formal prerequisite is invented. Data alternative uses advanced algorithms rather than placing Reinforcement Learning before a later neural-network foundation.
alternatives.distinctness: Academic priorities change from physical/ecological system modelling and robotics to inference, data management, learned predictors and geospatial/population evidence. Pairwise unique-course counts: 5; every pair exceeds the four-course floor.

alternatives.label: Mathematics, optimisation & economics
alternatives.labelReason: Reviewed completed mathematical/computational core and actual application weights; label describes these fields without claiming the full pure-mathematics sequence.
alternatives.concept: Combine calculus, probability, numerical methods and algorithms with optimisation, sequential decisions and economic modelling. Study uncertainty, market behaviour, public policy and investment appraisal through mathematical, statistical and computational approaches.
progression: All current term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass. Introductory programming precedes dependent algorithms and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes all dependent mathematics. Numerical methods and Linear Systems follow foundational mathematics. Some image-processing work precedes later matrix courses under the open curriculum; no extra formal prerequisite is invented. Data alternative uses advanced algorithms rather than placing Reinforcement Learning before a later neural-network foundation.
alternatives.distinctness: Academic priorities change from natural-system and statistical-learning applications to economic models, optimisation, sequential decisions and investment appraisal. Pairwise unique-course counts: 8, 7; every pair exceeds the four-course floor.

selection.assessment: Three evidence-backed programmes retained after current content and full schedule repair. The strongest response combines mathematical methods, proof and computational/applied modelling; data-oriented inference and economic optimisation change the academic priorities and actual courses. Pairwise differences are5,8and7courses, not arbitrary substitutions. Pure mathematics depth remains a material gap, but the mathematical core, algorithms and applications provide genuine programme-level comparability. Computer-science and physics stable directions remain explicit maximum-reached candidates; no formal double degree or fourth alternative is claimed.

blocks: Both explicitly teach sets, functions/relations, proof strategies and induction. UvA additionally develops number systems, cardinality and divisibility; this is partial correspondence.
Both study graphs and algorithms on networks. UCR emphasizes traversal, paths, trees and algorithmic complexity; UvA also develops graph-theoretic properties and colouring.
Both introduce Python programming for problem-solving. UvA applies it to mathematical experiments; UCR also develops recursion and object-oriented software.
Both develop single-variable differentiation and integration. UvA combines calculations with proof-oriented real analysis; UCR also uses computer algebra and dynamic models.
Both study vector spaces, linear maps, eigenvalues and orthogonality; UCR adds computational and statistical applications.
Both study computer-based solution of equations and numerical error. UCR offers a broader numerical-methods programme; UvA’s introduction includes SVD and sensitivity to small errors.
Both extend calculus to several variables. UCR’s description also supports differential equations and complex-valued functions, but not the complete proof/theorem structure of UvA analysis.

Both treat differential equations and stability. UCR concentrates on linear systems, signals and transforms; UvA additionally develops existence/uniqueness, nonlinear planar dynamics and periodic behaviour.
Both study probability spaces, conditional probability, random variables and distributions. UCR also includes inference and Monte Carlo methods.
Both examine ethical and societal questions around algorithms, AI, privacy and responsibility. UvA explicitly frames these questions through the profession and wider uses of mathematics.

Both implement mathematical models of population change using software. UCR’s ecological modelling is a smaller part of a broad ecology course; UvA centres disease ODE models, interventions and parameter estimation.
Both address estimation, tests and statistical inference. UCR develops applied multivariable models and diagnostics; UvA examines statistical procedures in a mathematical framework.
Group theory has no dedicated UCR counterpart; algebraic algorithms do not reproduce the study of groups and their structure.
Rings, ideals, field extensions and finite fields have no dedicated UCR counterpart.
The dedicated vector-field, surface-integral and Stokes-theorem course has no sufficiently documented separate UCR counterpart.
The course addresses theories of learning mathematics and mathematical communication; generic project reporting does not reproduce that educational function.
Topological spaces, compactness, homotopy and fundamental groups are not supplied by UCR’s applied modelling courses.
This is the twelve-credit Mathematics bachelor research project. UCR’s optional independent research is shown separately from its scheduled 180 credits.

notes.text: UvA provides a sustained proof-oriented sequence in analysis, abstract algebra, geometry and topology, followed by named advanced mathematics choices and a compulsory bachelor project. UCR offers meaningful calculus, linear algebra, proof and discrete reasoning, probability, numerical methods and linear systems with substantial computational applications. It does not reproduce that full pure-mathematics sequence. UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 credits.

audience.programmeDescription: The University of Amsterdam’s Mathematics bachelor builds a common foundation in proof, analysis, algebra, probability and mathematical skills, followed by advanced mathematics choices, free electives and an individual research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programmes develop mathematical and computational methods through modelling, data analysis or economic optimisation. UvA offers a more extensive pure-mathematics sequence, including abstract algebra, geometry, topology and advanced analysis. UCR’s proof and applied mathematical work provides real overlap while those differences remain substantial.
